k-hop subgraph via SparseTensor matrix power (C2, score 22)

inventory.name: PPR top-k subgraph extraction
inventory.counter_case: PPR requires full adjacency matrix and power iteration budget. Cortex knowledge graph is sparse entity-level — PPR density assumptions may not hold.

inventory.name: Import-fallback text search for edge discovery
inventory.counter_case: Text-based import matching is fragile — matches names in non-import contexts. Tree-sitter extracts imports more precisely; fallback adds noise when tree-sitter is available.

inventory.name: BFS radius expansion from search centers
inventory.counter_case: BFS in a code graph (call/import) differs from BFS in concept graph (usage/depends-on). Parallel implementations in Cortex share callers, not direct graph neighbors.

inventory.name: JSON-configured semantic expansion patterns
inventory.counter_case: Cortex graph edges already typed at entity level — JSON config adds maintenance overhead over simple BFS.

inventory.name: k-hop subgraph via SparseTensor matrix power
inventory.counter_case: TypeScript rewrite of SparseTensor ops is non-trivial; graphology adjacency lists may suffice at Cortex scale (<500 entities).

inventory.name: Swappable cosine vs MLP scoring decoder
inventory.counter_case: Cortex lacks entity ranking — swappable interface before any ranker exists is premature abstraction.

inventory.name: Dataset-level pickle caching
inventory.counter_case: Cortex already uses mtime-based stale detection; additional pickle cache duplicates state management.

inventory.name: Batched processing with .split(N)
inventory.counter_case: Cortex LLM calls are token-window-limited not GPU-memory-limited; .split() for GPU OOM doesn't translate to API throughput management.

inventory.name: Dual metric search (Euclidean / cosine toggle)
inventory.counter_case: Cortex does not use vector search in core path; applies only if semantic embedding added.

inventory.name: PyCG call graph + 2to3 auto-translation fallback
inventory.counter_case: PyCG and 2to3 are Python-specific; Cortex handles TypeScript. Pattern is valuable but not directly reusable.

inventory.name: Five-typed edge Code Property Graph
inventory.counter_case: Cortex entity graph is at module/class level; regraining to function/call-site level requires full re-ingestion redesign.

inventory.name: Hardcoded absolute paths for grammar/data
inventory.proposed_flaw_addition: Never hardcode data or model paths — derive from config or env var with local default.

inventory.name: Module-level hardcoded device = cuda:0
inventory.proposed_flaw_addition: Derive device from os.environ.get('DEVICE', 'cpu') or argparse argument.

inventory.name: LLMModel.__init__ missing self parameter
inventory.pattern: def __init__(model_name): — self absent, self.llm used inside
inventory.proposed_flaw_addition: Always exercise every class constructor in at least one test.

inventory.name: os.chdir() mutable global cwd
inventory.pattern: os.chdir() to set cwd for subprocess
inventory.proposed_flaw_addition: Pass cwd= to subprocess.run() instead of os.chdir().

inventory.name: PyCG complementary or redundant with tree-sitter for TypeScript?
inventory.question: Is there a TypeScript equivalent to PyCG (ts-morph? dependency-cruiser?) giving Cortex typed call edges?
alternatives: skip call graphs — entity graph sufficient

inventory.name: Should impact_analysis use PPR instead of BFS?
inventory.question: Should PPR from changed entity replace BFS in impact_analysis to surface most-affected entities first?
alternatives: BFS + sort by incoming-edge count as PPR proxy
